title: Tickeron AI flagged $GLSI before its 2-day, ~50% run on conferencenews with no new data. Would your model have chased day two?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Tickeron AI flagged Greenwich LifeSciences (GLSI,  
[https://tickeron.com/ticker/GLSI/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/GLSI/)) when two FLAMINGO-01 Phase III  
breast cancer abstracts were accepted for poster presentation at the  
San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium on Dec 9.  
  
Yesterday (Tue, Nov 17) GLSI jumped +36%, from $13.76 to $18.70.  
  
Today (Wed, Nov 18) it kept going, closing at $20.58, up another 10%.  
That's roughly +50% in two sessions.  
  
The model picked up a few things stacking on top of the abstract news.  
H.C. Wainwright reiterated its Buy rating and nudged its price target  
to $70. Sympathy buying hit peptide-based cancer vaccines after peer  
SELLAS Life Sciences (SLS, [https://tickeron.com/ticker/SLS/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/SLS/)) reported  
a successful Phase III readout. And the move was company-specific: the  
S&P 500 was lower and small-cap biotech was roughly flat. With about  
20% of the small float held short, short covering likely helped too.  
  
What's next: the Dec 9 poster sessions for efficacy and  
immune-response detail, and any financing after the rally.  
  
Full breakdown:  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-greenwich-lifesciences-glsi-stock-up-12-19-today-40395/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-greenwich-lifesciences-glsi-stock-up-12-19-today-40395/)  
  
Question for the AI traders here: on a small-cap biotech running on  
conference acceptance (not new data), does your model treat day-two  
follow-through as momentum to ride, or as a setup for a fade or  
dilution risk?
